[REG-02#001] Data Retention Schedule > Principle
Personal data is kept only as long as necessary for the purpose it was collected for, or as long as the law requires. Keeping data indefinitely is a breach of the storage limitation principle in the UK GDPR.

---

[REG-02#003] Data Retention Schedule > Reporting a suspected breach; Disposal; Review
Suspected breaches of this schedule, including data retained past its period or disposed of early, are reported to the Data Protection Lead within 72 hours.

At the end of the retention period, electronic records are deleted, including from backups at the next backup cycle rollover, and paper records are cross-cut shredded. Disposal of confidential waste is carried out under a certificate of destruction.

Deletion is not performed where a record is subject to an ongoing legal claim, investigation or regulatory request. In that case the record is placed on legal hold and the reason recorded.

The Data Protection Lead reviews this schedule annually against current legislation.

|---|---|---|

Every visitor must sign in at reception on arrival and sign out on departure. Visitors are issued with a numbered badge, which must be worn visibly at all times and returned on departure.

---

Pedestrians must keep to the green marked walkways. Where a walkway crosses a forklift aisle, pedestrians stop, make eye contact with the driver, and wait to be waved across. Never assume a driver has seen you.

The single-person lift limit is 20 kg. Loads above this require a second person or mechanical assistance. Trolleys and pallet trucks are available at each aisle end.

Assess the load before lifting: check the weight marking, test the load, keep it close to the body, bend the knees rather than the back, and avoid twisting.

Aisles and fire exits are kept clear at all times. Spillages are cleaned immediately and a wet floor sign placed. Broken pallets go to the designated skip, not against a wall.

---

Any employee may stop a task they believe to be unsafe without fear of consequence. Report the concern to the supervisor immediately.

---

Do not climb racking under any circumstances. Use the designated step ladders for the lower two levels.

The non-integrated man-riding cage is not for planned work. It may be used only for occasional, exceptional access where no suitable purpose-designed equipment is reasonably available, and only with a documented work-at-height assessment approved by the Warehouse Manager on the day.

Report damaged racking uprights or beams to the Warehouse Supervisor immediately and cordon off the bay. Damaged racking is not used until inspected.

---

[OPS-03#003] Refunds Standard Operating Procedure > Method
Refunds are made to the original payment method. Card refunds are processed by Finance through the payment gateway; the funds typically reach the customer's account three to five working days later, which is outside the company's control.

Trade customers are refunded by credit note against their account, not by bank transfer, unless the account is closed.

Refunds are never issued in cash, and never through petty cash.

This procedure covers the physical handling of returned goods: authorisation, receipt, inspection and disposition. The financial side, including when money is refunded and by what method, is covered separately in OPS-03.

No goods are accepted back without a Returns Authorisation number. Customer Services issues an RA number in the format RA-NNNNN, valid for 21 days.

Goods may be returned within 30 days of delivery if unused and in their original packaging. Consumer customers additionally have the statutory 14-day cancellation right under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013, which runs from the day after delivery and is not affected by the 30-day policy.

The following are not accepted for return unless faulty: bespoke engraved items, sharpened knives, and any item with broken hygiene seals.

The float is £250, held in the locked cash box in the Finance office. The Finance Assistant is the custodian. A second key is held by the Finance Manager.

| Rule | Limit |
|---|---|
| Maximum single transaction | £50 |
| Maximum per person per week | £100 |
| Items requiring Finance Manager approval | Any purchase above £25 |

Splitting a purchase into smaller amounts to stay under a limit is a disciplinary matter.

| 1 to 7 calendar days | Self-certification form on return |

Statutory Sick Pay is payable from the first qualifying day of absence. There are no longer any unpaid waiting days.

All employees qualify for Statutory Sick Pay regardless of their earnings. The Lower Earnings Limit no longer applies to sick pay, so part-time and lower-paid staff who were previously excluded are now covered.

Statutory Sick Pay is paid at the lower of the statutory weekly rate or 80 per cent of the employee's average weekly earnings. The statutory weekly rate for 2026/27 is £123.25.

Employees with more than 12 months of continuous service receive company sick pay at full salary for up to four weeks in any rolling 12-month period, inclusive of SSP. Company sick pay is discretionary and may be withheld where the absence procedure has not been followed.

The refund covers the price paid for the goods. Original outbound delivery is refunded where the customer is exercising a statutory cancellation right or where the goods were faulty, and is not refunded for a discretionary change-of-mind return.

Where disposition B has been recorded on a discretionary change-of-mind return, a deduction may be applied for the actual reduction in value caused by the customer handling the goods beyond what is necessary to establish their nature and function. question: What has to be checked on a forklift before a shift?

A documented pre-use check is completed at the start of every shift, before the truck is used, covering:

- Tyres, forks and mast for damage
- Hydraulic leaks
- Brakes, including the parking brake
- Horn, lights and beacon
- Battery charge and electrolyte level where applicable
- Seat belt condition and operation

Defects are recorded on the daily check sheet. A truck with a safety-critical defect is taken out of service, the key removed, and a "do not use" tag applied. Report to the Warehouse Supervisor immediately.

---

[OPS-06#004] Forklift Truck Operations > End of shift; Statutory inspection
Park in the designated bay, lower the forks fully, apply the parking brake, switch off, remove the key and return it to the key cabinet. Trucks on charge must have the charging area kept clear and ventilated.

Every truck receives a thorough examination under LOLER 1998. The interval is 12 months for trucks used only to lift loads, and 6 months for any truck fitted with a working platform or man-riding cage, because equipment used to lift people must be examined at the shorter interval. The two counterbalance trucks certified for use with the man-riding cage referred to in OPS-05 are therefore on the 6-month cycle. Certificates are held in the warehouse office.

---

[OPS-06#003] Forklift Truck Operations > Operating rules
- The seat belt must be worn at all times while the truck is in motion
- Maximum speed inside the building is 4 km/h
- Travel with the forks lowered approximately 100 mm from the floor and the mast tilted back
- Travel in reverse when the load obstructs forward vision
- Never lift or carry a passenger
- Never leave a truck unattended with the forks raised or the engine running
- Sound the horn at aisle ends, blind corners and the goods-in door

---

Pedestrians must keep to the green marked walkways. Where a walkway crosses a forklift aisle, pedestrians stop, make eye contact with the driver, and wait to be waved across. Never assume a driver has seen you.

The single-person lift limit is 20 kg. Loads above this require a second person or mechanical assistance. Trolleys and pallet trucks are available at each aisle end.

Assess the load before lifting: check the weight marking, test the load, keep it close to the body, bend the knees rather than the back, and avoid twisting.

---

On arrival the goods-in operative:

1. Checks the delivery note against the purchase order number
2. Counts pallets or cartons against the delivery note
3. Inspects for visible external damage before the driver leaves
4. Signs the driver's paperwork, noting any discrepancy or damage in writing

Only employees holding a current RTITB or equivalent accredited certificate for the relevant truck category, and who appear on the site authorised operator list, may operate a forklift. Authorisation is site-specific and issued in writing by the Warehouse Manager. Refresher training is required every three years.

The company operates three counterbalance trucks and two reach trucks. Authorisation is per category; a counterbalance certificate does not authorise reach truck operation.

Park in the designated bay, lower the forks fully, apply the parking brake, switch off, remove the key and return it to the key cabinet. Trucks on charge must have the charging area kept clear and ventilated.

Every truck receives a thorough examination under LOLER 1998. The interval is 12 months for trucks used only to lift loads, and 6 months for any truck fitted with a working platform or man-riding cage, because equipment used to lift people must be examined at the shorter interval. - Maximum speed inside the building is 4 km/h
- Travel with the forks lowered approximately 100 mm from the floor and the mast tilted back
- Travel in reverse when the load obstructs forward vision
- Never lift or carry a passenger

Pedestrians must keep to the green marked walkways. Where a walkway crosses a forklift aisle, pedestrians stop, make eye contact with the driver, and wait to be waved across. Never assume a driver has seen you.

The single-person lift limit is 20 kg. Loads above this require a second person or mechanical assistance. Trolleys and pallet trucks are available at each aisle end.

Assess the load before lifting: check the weight marking, test the load, keep it close to the body, bend the knees rather than the back, and avoid twisting.

The company operates three counterbalance trucks and two reach trucks. Authorisation is per category; a counterbalance certificate does not authorise reach truck operation.

Damage reports are acknowledged within two working days of being received.

Customer services raise a damage report and offer, at the customer's choice, a replacement despatched within one working day of the report being accepted, or a refund processed under OPS-03.

Damaged items are collected by the carrier or, for low-value items, the customer is asked to dispose of them. Do not return a damaged item without a Returns Authorisation number.

[CS-02#001] Damaged Goods Frequently Asked Questions > My order arrived damaged. What do I do?
Report it to customer services within 48 hours of delivery, on 01632 960 300 or support@northgate-kitchenware.invalid. Include the order number and photographs of the damage and the outer packaging.

Keep the packaging until the claim is settled. Carriers routinely require evidence of how the item was packed, and disposing of the box can invalidate the claim.

Repair, replacement, or refund, in that order of preference, at the company's discretion having regard to the customer's statutory rights. Where an item is out of stock or discontinued, a replacement of equivalent specification or a refund is offered.

The order number is sufficient for anything bought directly from us. Items bought through a third-party retailer are claimed through that retailer.

Check the packing note first, as orders short on stock are despatched as part shipments with the balance on back order. If the packing note lists an item that is not in the box, report it within 48 hours as above.

This procedure covers refunding money to customers. The physical handling and inspection of returned goods is covered in OPS-02.

Three routes exist and they are not interchangeable:

|---|---|---|
| Statutory cancellation | Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 | No. The deadline runs from receipt of the goods or from the customer's evidence of dispatch, whichever is earlier, so a refund may fall due before inspection is complete. |
| Faulty goods | Consumer Rights Act 2015 | Normally yes, but a short clear-cut fault must not be used to delay a refund beyond a reasonable period. |
| Discretionary change of mind | Company policy only | Yes. Disposition under OPS-02 must be recorded first. |

[CS-02#002] Damaged Goods Frequently Asked Questions > Why 48 hours?
The carrier's contract requires damage to be notified within three days. Reporting within 48 hours gives us time to raise the claim. Damage reported after this window is still considered, but the company may not be able to recover the cost from the carrier.

question: A new trade customer wants a credit account and next working day delivery. What do they need to do?
prompt:
You are an assistant answering questions about an organisation's internal policies and procedures.

Rules:
1. Answer using only the evidence provided. Do not use outside knowledge.
2. Cite the identifier in square brackets, for example [HR-13#001], after every statement you make.

4. Be concise. Do not add advice that is not in the evidence.

EVIDENCE:
[FIN-01#002] Invoicing and Credit Control > Credit accounts
New trade customers apply for a credit account using the account application form. Finance obtains a credit reference and takes two trade references before an account is opened. Opening limits are typically £2,500, reviewed after six months of trading.

Credit limit increases are approved by the Finance Manager up to £15,000, and by the Managing Director above that.

---

[OPS-01#002] Order Processing Standard Operating Procedure > 2. Credit check
Trade orders are automatically held if the customer's account balance exceeds their credit limit or if any invoice is more than 45 days overdue, in line with the credit control stages in FIN-01. Held orders appear on the credit control queue and are released only by Finance under FIN-01.

---

[OPS-04#001] Stock Intake Standard Operating Procedure > Booking in
Suppliers must book a delivery slot in advance through the goods-in email address. Deliveries arriving without a booked slot are accepted only if a bay is free, and may be turned away during peak periods.

Delivery slots run from 07:30 to 16:00, Monday to Friday. No inbound deliveries are accepted on Saturdays.

---

[FIN-01#001] Invoicing and Credit Control > Invoicing
Invoices are raised automatically on despatch and emailed to the address held on the customer account. Paper invoices are issued only on request.

Standard payment terms are 30 days from the date of invoice. Terms are stated on the invoice and in the customer's account agreement.

---

[CS-11#001] Delivery Frequently Asked Questions > How long does delivery take?
These terms replace CS-01 with effect from 1 February 2026, following the annual carrier tender.

Standard delivery is 3 to 5 working days from despatch. Next working day delivery is available on orders placed and paid before 14:00, Monday to Thursday. Orders placed after 14:00 on Thursday for next-day delivery arrive on Monday, as the carrier does not deliver at weekends.

---

[FIN-01#004] Invoicing and Credit Control > Disputes; Bad debt
A customer disputing an invoice must raise it within 14 days. Finance logs the dispute, and the disputed amount only is placed on hold. The undisputed balance remains payable on the original terms.

Debts referred to the collection agency and unrecovered after six months are written off with Managing Director approval, and the customer account is closed to credit.
